newsitem.title: ESTONIA: SOCCER-SWEDEN TAKE NARROW 3-2 WIN FROM ESTONIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SWEDEN TAKE NARROW 3-2 WIN FROM ESTONIA.

text.p: Sweden survived a fright in the final minutes of their World Cup European zone group four soccer qualifier on Sunday against Estonia, taking away a narrow 3-2 win after late Estonian pressure.
Sweden stay third in the group after the win as Austria maintained the second spot following a 3-1 defeat of a Latvian side reduced to 10 men after 39 minutes on the same night.

The Swedes are on 12 points from six games in the group while Austria are on 13 from six. Both have games in hand on group leader Scotland, who earlier beat Belarus 1-0 to give them 17 points from eight matches.
Sweden, as expected from the more experienced side, came out fighting in the first half with Borussia Moenchengladbach striker Martin Dahlin opening the scoring after 13 minutes.
He received a ball knocked down during a scramble in the Estonian box and slipped it past Estonian goalkeeper Mart Poom.
From that point on in the first half, Poom, who plays for English league side Derby, had to work hard.
In the 26th minute, Sweden's Par Zetterberg shot over the bar after another scramble in the box while Hakan Mild had a chance three minutes later as he headed over the net.

Off-target shots and Poom's efforts managed to frustrate the Swedes for the rest of the first half. They were forced to wait until the 53rd minute when Zetterberg, brought down in the box, converted a penalty.

Bologna striker Kennet Andersson seemed to seal an easy victory for the Swedes when he received a ball onto his chest just yards (metres) away from the goal in the 73rd minute and vollied it past Poom.
But the Estonians fought back in the final minutes, taking advantage of what seemed to be a tired Swedish team.
Estonian midfielder Andres Oper got behind the Swedish defence as he received a cross from the left wing, firing it passed Swedish goalkeeper Magnus Hedman in the 75th minute.
With renewed vigour, the Estonian team kept the pressure on, hoping to humiliate their more distinguished visitors.
Estonian striker Marko Kristal shocked the Swedes again in the 85th, when his constant harrying runs against the Swedish defence finally struck gold.
He darted through into shooting distance and hit a hard shot straight past Hedman for Estonia's second.

Estonia - 1-Mart Poom, 2-Marek Lemsalu, 3-Urmas Kirs, 4-Sergei Hohlov-Simson, 5-Janek Meet, 6-Liivo Leetma (18-Kristen Viikmae 45), 7-Meelis Rooba (14-Mati Pari 66), 8-Andres Oper, 9-Marko Kristal, 10-Martin Reim, 11-Indrek Zelinksi.

Sweden: 1-Magnus Hedman, 2-Roland Nilsson, 3-Patrik Andersson, 4-Joachim Bjorklund, 5-Gary Sundgren, 6-Hakan Mild (Niclas Alexandersson 73), 7-Par Zetterberg, 8-Andreas Andersson, 9-Jonas Thern, 10-Martin Dahlin (20-Joergen Pettersson), 11-Kennet Andersson (15-Andreas Jacobsson 85).
